page0.text:
"Thank you for the meal."
"Thanks for the meal."
We mutually thank our cook.
"I'm glad you both enjoyed it. You really ate everything down to the last speck."

page1.text:
Sakura starts cleaning up.
On the dining table are a clay pot, three bowls, and all the garnishes you would need for udon.

page2.text:
"Oh, let me clean up. My fever's better, so it's the least I can do."
"Really? Then I'll ask you to help a little to see how much you've recovered. I can wash the dishes, so please bring the dirty dishes over and clean up around the table."

page3.text:
Sakura puts on her apron and moves to the kitchen.
I'll bring the clay pot and bowls over, then.

page4.text:
"Shirou, are you feeling all right? You said your fever has improved, but you still don't look well."
"Huh? Am I still pale?"

page5.text:
"...Hm. Not quite pale, but unwell.
Your magical energy, which could be said to be your lifeline as a Master—as a mage—is still lacking. I don't recall the battle last night placing an undue burden on you, but the enemy might have placed some contrivance to drain your energy in the temple grounds."

page6.text:
"Hmm..."
Now that she mentions it, Ryudou Temple did feel off, somehow.
All the people inside were weakened, so maybe Caster set up a Bounded Field to drain life energy from humans inside.

page7.text: "I'm feeling better now, so it's no problem. My magical energy will come back if I get nutrition. My energy capacity isn't much to sneeze at anyway, so I'm sure it'll fill back up once I eat dinner."

page8.text:
"You know yourself best, so I won't press the issue if you say so. Sakura is right, though. You do take your own condition too lightly."
Saber stacks the three bowls while saying that.

page9.text:
"I just need to give these to Sakura, yes? I'll also carry the pot, so please clean the table, Shirou."
She heads to the kitchen without waiting for my reply.

page10.text:
"Sakura, should I put the bowls here?"
"Oh, Saber? Yes, you can set the dirty dishes down there."
"I see. Also, lunch was delicious. I must thank you again."
"Ahaha, I still have a lot to learn. Senpai's the one who's really good at making porridge and udon noodles."

page11.text:
"..."
I hear a cheerful conversation from the kitchen.
"Hey, those two get along pretty well after all."
Maybe they hit it off when they were cleaning up after breakfast.
Anyway, it's good to see them get along.
